Ladies and gentlemen, the Compromiso de Sevilla, the outcome document of this conference, is an important landmark on the path to the SDGs. It shows that multilateralism is very much alive, despite the challenges that we're facing. And it underlines what we can achieve when we work closely together. But the work is not done yet. Now it's, of course, the time to implement what we have agreed in the compromise. Domestic revenue mobilization or DRM, is key. Higher domestic revenues can close a large part of the SDG financing gap. Effective and progressive tax systems are needed around the world. Germany is staying committed to supporting DRM and combating tax evasion globally. Currently, we are supporting 30 partner countries in mobilizing additional tax revenues. Strengthening tax policies and administration is one of the most cost-effective investments in development cooperation. Every dollar invested in this way brings several times the amount in domestic funds. This is especially important in times of shrinking ODA budgets in many countries. In this context, the Addis Tax Initiative's Seville Declaration on DRM is certainly timely. It renews and strengthens our joint commitment to step up our support for DRM. And it boosts the renewed framework on DRM set out in the outcome document on this conference. We, the lead implementing countries of the Civil Declaration, call upon all stakeholders to join the Addis Tax Initiative, ATI, and support the new declaration. The ATI has proven its value. In the recent years, more than two out of three ATI partner countries have successfully raised their revenues, for example, Senegal, Ghana, Mauritania, and Indonesia. They have expanded their tax base and increased their tax to GDP ratio. They can now invest more in public goods like health, education, and climate protection. As co-initiator, Germany has always been a strong supporter of the ATAI, and Germany will remain so in the future. The Civil Declaration provides a strong foundation for our future work because it focuses more on more than quantitative targets. It also addresses important issues of justice and solidarity. It emphasizes gender equality and environmental protection as important aspects of tax policy. And it strengthens international tax cooperation and the taxation of the super-rich. Ultimately, national governments can only combat tax evasion if the international tax system is also effective and fair. Together, we must ensure that everybody, including multinational companies and the super-rich, pay their fair shares in taxes. Germany stands ready to move this agenda forward. Thank you very much.
